newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia's Costello sees no company tax hike.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia's Costello sees no company tax hike.

text.p: Australian Treasurer Peter Costello said on Wednesday he saw no need to raise the company tax rate.
Asked on Perth radio 6PR whether there was a need to look at raising the company tax rate, Costello said: "No, because that's already been done. That was already done as from the 1995/96 year."
Former Labor Prime Minister Paul Keating raised the company tax rate to 36 percent from 33 percent in the 1995/96 budget.

On Tuesday, the government's mid-year budget review showed the 1996/97 budget outlook had worsened by almost A$3.0 billion and revealed that the government would need to look for further savings in the 1997/98 year.
The government is now forecasting an underlying budget deficit of A$8.5 billion in the 1996/97 year, compared with the A$5.6 billion forecast in the August budget.
On Tuesday, Costello said company tax collection, one of the government's largest sources of revenue, was running siginificantly below budget estimates.
